summary: Data supply chains and evaluations for audio, video and emerging AI modalities.
editor_note: The sharper bet is a programmable supply chain for perceptual data, not another annotation marketplace: Mundo coordinates real-world organizations, domain experts and quality controls to produce multilingual audio, video and emerging-modality datasets. Named customers and exclusivity are investor-reported, while rights, consent and repeatable quality across distributed suppliers remain the central risks.
why_featured: $20M Series A for perceptual AI data
investors: GreatPoint Ventures, Y Combinator, Next Frontier Capital, E12 Ventures

sources.label: Vancouver Tech Journal Series A report

product_evidence.claim: Mundo supplies data and evaluations across audio, video and emerging modalities for teams building perceptual AI systems.
The company coordinates real-world organizations into data supply nodes and iterates those supply chains as model requirements change.

market_context.primary_user: Frontier AI labs and research teams building multimodal models.
market_context.differentiation: Builds repeatable data supply chains from real-world organizations instead of relying only on scraped web data or one-off freelancer collection.
market_context.why_now: Speech, video and embodied systems need fresh domain-specific sensory data and evaluations that open-web text cannot provide.

risks.claim: Customer names, supplier exclusivity and demand are investor-reported; scaling rights, consent and consistent quality across distributed suppliers remains unproven publicly.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment based on Mundo and GreatPoint Ventures materials.
